state.misconception_label: Does not know the properties of a rectangle

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The angles highlighted on this rectangle with different length sides can never be... ![A rectangle with the diagonals drawn in. The angle on the right hand side at the centre is highlighted in red and the angle at the bottom at the centre is highlighted in yellow.](). I got acute because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a rectangular piece of paper and you fold it in half along both diagonals. What do you notice about the angles where the diagonals intersect? This can help us understand why the angles highlighted on the rectangle with different length sides can never be equal.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see what you mean... so when I fold the paper along the diagonals, the angles where they cross in the middle aren't all the same? But I'm still a bit confused - does that mean the red and yellow angles are different from each other, or are they different from the corner angles of the rectangle?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a rectangular piece of paper and you fold it along the diagonal. What do you notice about the sides that are created when you fold it? This can help us understand why the angles at the center of the rectangle with different length sides can never be equal.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses vague folding metaphors that don't directly address the student's confusion about which angles are equal, the domain accuracy is questionable (the prompt about folding along 'the diagonal' in Turn 3 is unclear), and the student shows increased confusion rather than improvement by Turn 2.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, hands-on analogies (folding rectangular paper along diagonals) to help the student understand the abstract geometric properties of angles formed by diagonals in a rectangle.
